channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Fiocruz terá produção nacional de terapias celulares contra o câncer
item.description: Fiocruz launched the Center for Development and Production of CAR-T Therapies, enabling national production of advanced cell therapies for leukemia, lymphoma, and myeloma at reduced costs for the SUS. Part of the Novo PAC with R$330 million invested, the initiative positions Brazil as one of the few countries capable of offering this high-tech treatment free of charge through its public health system. President Lula attended the event, emphasizing the role of science and SUS in curing patients like Paulo Peregrino, who was successfully treated in 2022.

item.title: Lula pede para governador do Rio prender “ladrões” e “milicianos” que comandaram estado
item.description: President Lula urged acting Rio de Janeiro Governor Ricardo Couto to arrest the 'thieves' and 'militiamen' who governed the state in recent years, particularly those tied to former Governor Cláudio Castro’s faction. He emphasized that Couto, who assumed office after Castro’s resignation without being elected, has a unique six-month window to enact meaningful change before the October elections. Lula stressed that Rio, a globally renowned city, must not be ruled by organized crime, and its people deserve better than militia-led governance.

item.title: Ao lado de Lula, Padilha chama Flávio de “poderoso chefão” dos hospitais do RJ
item.description: Health Minister Alexandre Padilha accused Senator Flávio Bolsonaro of allowing federal hospitals in Rio de Janeiro to be controlled by militias during the Bolsonaro government, describing him as a 'powerful boss' who dictated appointments and contracts. Padilha cited specific examples, including illegal parking fees at Cardoso Fontes Hospital and the closure of ICU units during the pandemic, asserting Flávio’s direct responsibility for these actions.

item.title: Aliado de Lula chama Neymar de “vagabundo”, mas diz que vai torcer por ele
item.description: Federal deputy André Janones (Rede-MG), an ally of President Lula, called Neymar a 'vagabundo' with no political understanding or values, yet said he will cheer for him as a football player, condemning the left's 'intellectual elitism' that rejected Neymar over his 2022 Bolsonaro support. While the left ignored Neymar's national team call-up, the PT emphasized the quest for a sixth World Cup, with Lula featured kissing the trophy in social media posts. The Neymar controversy highlights the ideological divide between bolsonaristas and petists ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro posta vídeo associando Deolane a Lula
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro posted a video linking Deolane Bezerra, arrested in Operation Vérnix on suspicion of money laundering for the PCC, to President Lula, implying this explains his reluctance to classify factions as terrorist groups. The post includes images of Deolane with Lula and her statement that she 'likes to defend criminals'. Justice upheld her preventive detention and froze R$ 27 million in her name.

item.title: 38% avaliam governo Lula como “ruim” e 32% como “bom”, diz Datafolha
item.description: President Lula's government has 38% negative and 32% positive ratings, with fluctuations within the margin of error since April. Approval and disapproval of the president are tied at 48% each. The Datafolha survey interviewed 2,004 voters aged 16 or older across 139 municipalities between May 20 and 21, 2026.

item.title: A hora e a vez de Michelle Bolsonaro
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro, former first lady, remains distant from her stepson Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign despite her electoral strength among women and evangelicals, backing opposition candidates in states like Ceará and Santa Catarina. Though she has reduced political activity to care for Jair Bolsonaro’s health, she remains focused on her own Senate bid in the DF and strengthening trusted allies, waiting for potential internal setbacks.

item.title: “Mais uma derrota de Moraes”, diz Eduardo Bolsonaro sobre soltura de Zambelli na Itália
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro celebrated the Italian court's decision to annul the extradition of former deputy Carla Zambelli to Brazil, calling it another defeat for Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes. He claimed Moraes has failed to extradite anyone in Italy, Spain, Argentina, or the U.S., and framed Zambelli as a political prisoner. Zambelli had been detained in Italy since July 2025 after being convicted for invading the CNJ's system.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro não comparece à Marcha para Jesus no Rio
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) canceled his participation in the March for Jesus in Rio de Janeiro due to commitments in Brasília, according to his office. His presence had been expected as part of a strategy to bolster his presidential pre-campaign through religious events. The absence may reduce his visibility among evangelical voters, a key demographic in his electoral ambitions.

item.title: No RJ, Lula faz apelo a Couto: ‘trabalhe para prender todos os ladrões que governaram esse estado’.
item.description: President Lula appealed to Rio de Janeiro's acting governor, Ricardo Couto, to fight organized crime and imprison the 'thieves who governed the state,' including deputies linked to militias. He praised the judiciary's decision to keep Couto in office after Cláudio Castro's resignation and criticized the possibility of Legislative Assembly appointment, fearing they would choose a militiaman. The remarks were made during the inauguration of Fiocruz's new Technological Development Center in Health.

item.title: Padilha diz que Flávio era “poderoso chefão” de hospitais no RJ
item.description: Health Minister Alexandre Padilha accused Senator Flávio Bolsonaro of acting as a 'powerful boss' over federal health institutions in Rio de Janeiro during Jair Bolsonaro’s administration, appointing directors, selecting contracts, closing ICUs during the pandemic, and handing over the Cardoso Fontes Federal Hospital to militias. Padilha also criticized the former president for mocking covid-19 patients. Flávio Bolsonaro’s office did not respond to requests for comment.

item.title: Em evento em SP, pré-candidatos da direita criticam polarização e defendem nova agenda para o país
item.description: Right-wing pre-candidates Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), Renan Santos (Missão) and Aldo Rebelo (DC) gathered in Guarujá (SP) to advocate for economic reforms, anti-corruption and anti-violence measures, and to criticize political polarization, calling for a reorganization of the branches of government and limits on judicial activism. Caiado joined via video, stating that defeating the PT requires a government of deliveries with popular approval. The candidates emphasized Brazil’s need to become globally competitive and to reduce public spending to restore fiscal credibility.

item.title: Renan vê decepcionados com Flávio e apela a discurso radical à direita
item.description: Renan Santos, a presidential pre-candidate from the Missão party, stated that Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) is experiencing natural wear in the presidential race and aims to attract right-wing voters disappointed with Bolsonarism. In a radical speech in Guarujá (SP), he attacked the Bolsonaro family, advocated for harsher criminal penalties, and positioned himself as an alternative to both the Workers' Party (PT) and traditional right-wing politics.

item.title: Sem presença de Flávio Bolsonaro, Marcha para Jesus ocorre neste sábado no Rio
item.description: The March for Jesus in Rio de Janeiro took place without Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who remained in Brasília to prepare for a potential meeting with Donald Trump. His absence was seen as a reaction to a Datafolha poll showing 64% of voters viewed his request for funding from Daniel Vorcaro for the 'Dark Horse' film as inappropriate, though allies like Sóstenes Cavalcante and Silas Malafaia downplayed the poll’s significance.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro registra boletim de ocorrência nos EUA por importunação
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro filed a police report in the U.S. after claiming a suspicious individual harassed his family in Texas, including his 5-year-old daughter. He alleges the man is linked to The Intercept and had inquired about his routine, suggesting ties to the PCC. The former deputy described the incident as an attempt to intimidate and terrorize his family.

item.title: Lula diz a governador interino para prender ‘ladrões’ e ‘milicianos’ que comandaram o Estado do RJ
item.description: Lula praised Rio de Janeiro's interim governor, Judge Ricardo Couto, urging him to arrest 'thieves' and 'militiamen' who governed the state, pledging federal support to combat organized crime. The remarks were made at the inauguration of Fiocruz's CDTS in Rio, following the resignation of Cláudio Castro.

item.title: Advogado Daniel Bialski surge nos bastidores como nome cotado para defesa de Vorcaro
item.description: Criminal lawyer Daniel Bialski is being discussed behind the scenes as a potential new defense attorney for banker Daniel Vorcaro in the Master case, following the departure of José Luis Oliveira Lima (Juca). The move reflects the need for a lawyer with access to STF Minister André Mendonça, the case's rapporteur, amid the rejection of Vorcaro's plea deal proposal and increasing pressure on him, as he reportedly considers raising the restitution amount from R$40 billion to R$60 billion.

item.title: Integrantes da campanha de Lula dizem que pacote pesou na melhora da avaliação do governo
item.description: Allies of Lula's re-election campaign attribute the improvement in government approval to a recent package of positive measures, including Desenrola 2.0, the abolition of the 'blusinhas' tax, and fuel subsidies, alongside negative media coverage of Flávio Bolsonaro and Daniel Vorcaro. They state that the government has overcome the negative news cycle of early 2024, and that declining disapproval is directly tied to Lula's proactive agenda, including international trips and new credit lines for transport workers.

item.title: Brasil não é menor nem menos competitivo do que ninguém, diz Lula
item.description: President Lula stated at the inauguration of the new headquarters of the Technological Development Center in Health at Fiocruz that Brazil is neither smaller nor less competitive than any other country, provided it dares to invest in research and technology. He argued that the cost of not conducting research outweighs the investment, likening it to oil exploration, and stressed the center’s role in advancing vaccines, medicines, and technologies for the SUS. The new 15,000-square-meter facility will serve as a health innovation hub, connecting researchers, universities, and national and international partners.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro na casa de Vorcaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro visited Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, shortly after Vorcaro's release from prison with an electronic ankle monitor. The following day, according to journalist Igor Gadelha of Metrópoles, Flávio was announced as a presidential candidate for the 2026 election.

item.title: Aprovação de governo perdeu peso como fator decisivo para ganhar eleição
item.description: Government approval has lost weight as a decisive factor in the 2026 elections, with Lula's net approval dropping from 11 points in April to just six points by May 13, according to Datafolha. With a two-point margin of error, approval and disapproval are technically tied at 48%, indicating erosion of the government's image as a key electoral asset.

item.title: Envolvimento de Flávio com banqueiro do Master alimenta divisão entre os evangélicos
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's request for funding from banker Daniel Vorcaro to finance a film about his father has deepened divisions among evangelical leaders, with some backing former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado and others viewing Michelle Bolsonaro as a potential alternative. Despite the controversy, religious leaders believe most evangelicals will unite behind a candidate endorsed by Jair Bolsonaro in a potential runoff.

item.title: PL está enredado nos maus lençóis da família Bolsonaro
item.description: The article criticizes Jair Bolsonaro for his failed policies, particularly pandemic denialism and efforts to retain power through illegal means. Now, the strategy of nominating his eldest son as a presidential candidate for 2026 is under scrutiny and may collapse amid mounting legal and political pressures.

item.title: Como o último Datafolha frustrou petistas e trouxe más notícias a Lula
item.description: The latest Datafolha poll shows Lula leading Flávio Bolsonaro 47% to 43% in a simulated runoff, with Lula gaining two points and Flávio losing two since the previous survey. Despite negative news about Flávio involving former banker Daniel Vorcaro, the damage was less than expected, and Lula’s high rejection rate continues to hinder his recovery. Scandals like Master and INSS threaten the government, while the opposition seeks to capitalize on discontent with agendas such as classifying criminal factions as terrorists.

item.title: Lula: "Disse a Trump que Brasil não dá preferência nem aos EUA nem à China"
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that Brazil has no preference for any country in international relations, specifically mentioning the United States and China, and emphasized that it prioritizes partners willing to transfer technology to Brazil. He made these remarks during the inauguration of the Technological Development Center in Health at Fiocruz in Rio de Janeiro, highlighting Brazil's commitment to national sovereignty and multilateralism.

item.title: Pré-candidato do Missão, Renan ataca Pablo Marçal, Lula e Bolsonaro
item.description: Renan Santos, pre-candidate of the Missão party linked to MBL, attacked Pablo Marçal, Lula, and Bolsonaro at an event in Guarujá, positioning himself as an alternative to the political system. He called Marçal a 'fool' and 'fraudster', claimed he would defeat Lula in debates, and labeled Bolsonaro a 'complete idiot', while also accusing Flávio Bolsonaro of involvement in scandals.

item.title: Governo Lula dobra gasto com anúncios no Instagram e Facebook
item.description: The Lula government doubled its spending on Instagram and Facebook ads, reaching R$21 million from January to mid-May 2025, up from R$11.45 million in the same period of 2024. The ads promoted federal programs and actions, according to Meta's ad library data published by Estadão.

item.title: Vídeo feito com IA lança candidatura de Joaquim Barbosa à presidência
item.description: An AI-generated video released by the Christian Democracy party presents Joaquim Barbosa as a potential presidential candidate in 2026, sparking debate over the campaign's legitimacy and exposing internal party divisions, particularly after the expulsion of Aldo Rebelo, who had previously announced his pre-candidacy. Barbosa, renowned for his role as rapporteur in the Mensalão trial at the STF, is seen as a symbol of strictness against white-collar corruption and could become one of the few Black candidates to run for president in Brazil's history.

item.title: Trabalhe para prender ladrões que governaram o RJ, diz Lula a Couto
item.description: At the inauguration of the CDTS headquarters at Fiocruz in Rio de Janeiro, President Lula urged interim Governor Ricardo Couto to work toward arresting the 'thieves who governed the state' and lawmakers tied to an organized militia, advocating for the reclamation of territory for the people. He endorsed the judicial decision to keep Couto in office after Claudio Castro’s resignation and reaffirmed federal support in combating organized crime, linking the effort to the pending approval of the Public Security PEC, which has passed the Chamber and awaits Senate vote.

item.title: Trabalhe para prender ladrões que governaram o Rio, diz Lula a interino
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva urged the acting governor of Rio de Janeiro, Judge Ricardo Couto, to take stronger action against militias and organized crime in the state. Lula emphasized the need to imprison the thieves who governed Rio, referring to criminal groups and potential links to corrupt public policies. The statement was made on Saturday, May 23, 2026, during a political event.

item.title: Governo Lula articula nova operação de ajuda a Cuba
item.description: The Lula government is coordinating a new humanitarian aid shipment to Cuba in joint action with Spain and Mexico through the World Food Programme (PMA) to optimize freight costs for food and medicine. Brazil has already sent two shipments in 2026 but denies energy aid due to the risk of U.S. sanctions on Petrobras, which could worsen domestic fuel price increases. The operation is coordinated by the Brazilian Cooperation Agency (ABC) under Itamaraty and seeks to channel part of the aid through UN bodies to avoid sanctions, following a model already adopted by Spain.

item.title: 'Precisamos orar pela nação': concentração da 19ª Marcha para Jesus reúne fiéis no Centro do Rio
item.description: The 19th March for Jesus gathered thousands of believers in downtown Rio de Janeiro on President Vargas Avenue, with an expected 300,000 attendees and 40,000 at the Sambadrome. Held during an election year under the theme 'The Power of Decision', the event featured speeches linking faith and politics, including organizer Viviane Dias stating the need to 'pray for the nation'. The march included gospel performances, street vendors selling Brazilian and Israeli flags, and multigenerational participation, such as twins Raquel and Ruth Xavier, who have attended every edition since the first.

item.title: Após polêmicas, Virginia comemora engajamento: “Glória a Deus”
item.description: Virginia Fonseca celebrated being the second most engaged Brazilian personality on social media for the week, behind only Neymar Jr., following controversies over her zoo visit in Dubai and racism allegations. She posted a message of thanks saying 'All honor and glory to God. 2026 is ours', which was interpreted as an indirect reference to the 2026 elections, despite her not being a candidate.

item.title: Aldo defende aumento da base tributária; Renan, corte de gastos, em debate entre pré-candidatos
item.description: Presidential pre-candidates Aldo Rebelo and Renan Santos debated on Saturday how to curb the advance of public debt. Aldo advocated for increasing the tax base, while Renan argued for cutting public spending.

item.title: Queremos trabalhar com quem quer trabalhar com transferência de tecnologia, diz Lula
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that Brazil's challenge is to start asking 'how much does it cost not to act' in order for the country to join the ranks of developed nations, emphasizing the importance of technology transfer and partnerships with those willing to collaborate. Speaking at an event on Saturday, the 23rd, he stressed the need for investment in innovation and technological development to drive national growth.

item.title: No Rio, Lula faz aceno a governador em exercício e diz que se a Alerj tivesse que indicar alguém para o cargo 'viria um miliciano'
item.description: Lula praised Rio de Janeiro's acting governor, Ricardo Couto, for not being a career politician and for being appointed by the Judiciary, stating that if the state legislature (Alerj) had to appoint someone, 'it would be a milician'. He reiterated his commitment to public safety and health, emphasizing investments in technology and federal partnerships to combat militias and strengthen the SUS in the state.

item.title: Para 48%, Flávio deveria desistir depois de acerto com Vorcaro
item.description: A Datafolha poll from May 2026 shows 48% of voters believe Senator Flávio Bolsonaro should withdraw from the presidential race following allegations he solicited funds from banker Daniel Vorcaro, while 44% support maintaining his candidacy — a technical tie within the margin of error. Among Bolsonaro’s supporters, 88% favor continuation, and 64% judge his conduct as inappropriate in seeking money from Vorcaro, founder of Banco Master.

item.title: Barroso: ‘Tem alguma decisão do STF favorecendo o Banco Master? Não que eu saiba’
item.description: Former Supreme Court President Luís Roberto Barroso defended the institution amid suspicions of ministerial involvement in the Banco Master case, stating he is unaware of any STF decision favoring the bank. He acknowledged that a set of facts has led to negative public perception but stressed the need to avoid premature judgment and await investigation outcomes, distinguishing personal critiques from institutional integrity.

item.title: Ibaneis Rocha se isola de Jair Bolsonaro, Michelle, Damares, Celina…
item.description: Ibaneis Rocha (MDB) has lost political support following the scandal involving the attempted purchase of Banco Master by BRB, which alienated the Bolsonaro family and allies like Damares Alves. He has fallen to third place in Senate race polls for the Federal District, while Michelle Bolsonaro leads with 29.8%. Isolated and facing a growing rift with his former running mate Celina Leão, Ibaneis is under pressure to abandon his Senate bid and run for the Chamber of Deputies instead.

item.title: Justiça dos EUA autoriza notificação de Moraes por e-mail
item.description: A U.S. Federal Court in Florida authorized Rumble and Trump Media & Technology Group to notify Brazilian Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes by email in a lawsuit filed in the United States. The case, initiated in 2025, challenges Moraes' orders removing profiles of Bolsonaro supporters from the platforms, claiming violations of the First Amendment. The plaintiffs argued formal channels in Brazil were 'blocked,' and Moraes now has up to 30 days to respond or face a default judgment.

item.title: No RJ, Lula diz a governador para prender 'ladrões' e 'milicianos' que comandaram o estado
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva urged Rio de Janeiro's interim governor, Ricardo Couto, to combat organized crime and imprison 'thieves' and 'militiamen' who have dominated the state's politics in recent years. Lula stressed that Rio, despite being the 'most famous city in the world,' cannot be overtaken by crime and said the federal government will support public security actions, including approving the law to confront criminal factions and recreating the Ministry of Public Security, contingent on Senate approval of the PEC.

item.title: Aldo Rebelo contesta expulsão do partido e diz que continua fazendo pré-campanha
item.description: Aldo Rebelo claims he remains affiliated with the Christian Democracy party and continues his presidential pre-campaign, despite the party's national leadership announcing his summary expulsion on Friday. He states he was not officially notified and calls the decision unconstitutional and abusive, promising to take the case to court. Rebelo also challenges the legitimacy of Joaquim Barbosa's pre-candidacy, saying the former STF minister only sent a message via a journalist and that no one knows if Barbosa is even in Brazil.

item.title: Filiado ao PL, Mendonça Filho diz que não vai se opor à aliança de aliada com Lula
item.description: Mendonça Filho, federal deputy from PL-PE, stated he does not oppose Governor Raquel Lyra's (PSD) rapprochement with President Lula, arguing that dialogue between political forces is part of state leadership. He emphasized that Lyra must govern for Pernambuco and maintain federal partnerships regardless of the ruling party. The comment comes amid João Campos' (PSB) efforts to nationalize the 2026 state election campaign and prevent a dual slate for Lula in the state.

item.title: Perfil ligado ao DC lança Joaquim Barbosa candidato à Presidência
item.description: An Instagram profile linked to the DC party released an AI-generated video announcing Joaquim Barbosa as a 2026 presidential candidate. Barbosa, former STF minister and rapporteur of the Mensalão trial, criticized the polarization between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. The announcement sparked internal conflict in the DC, as Aldo Rebelo challenged the candidacy and faces disciplinary action for defying party leadership.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro diz que foi “importunado” em sua casa nos EUA
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro said he was disturbed at his Texas home by someone linked to Intercept Brasil, which had released an audio of his brother Flávio Bolsonaro asking for money from Daniel Vorcaro. He called the police, filed a report, and denied that his comment about guns was a threat, stressing the incident was abnormal and that he will not tolerate harassment against his family.

item.title: Ancelotti vira exemplo para Caiado
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, governor of Goiás, left office with nearly 90% approval, a rare achievement in the social media era. In an interview with Papo Antagonista, he emphasized his readiness to run for president in 2026, citing Carlo Ancelotti as a model of leadership and consistency. The post suggests Caiado sees the Real Madrid coach as a political role model to emulate.

item.title: “Adotem um deputado, um senador”, diz chairman da Esfera a empresários
item.description: João Camargo, chairman of Esfera Brasil, called Brazil's economic performance over the last eight years 'shameful,' noting the country's stock market share relative to the U.S. dropped from 3.3% to 1.5%. He urged business leaders to 'adopt' federal deputies and senators, hold them accountable, and financially support their campaigns, rejecting polarization and advocating for state policies. Camargo also criticized the imprisonment of former presidents and stressed the need for concrete proposals in the 2026 presidential election.

item.title: Datafolha: rejeição a Lula cai para 38%, mas segue acima da aprovação
item.description: The Datafolha poll shows Lula's government rejection dropped to 38% while approval rose to 32%, narrowing the gap between negative and positive evaluations. His personal approval is tied at 48% approve and 48% disapprove. In electoral scenarios, Lula leads Flávio Bolsonaro by nine points in the first round (40% to 31%) and holds a 47% to 43% advantage in a potential runoff.

item.title: Datafolha aponta leve melhora na avaliação de Lula após caso “Dark Horse”
item.description: The Datafolha poll shows a slight improvement in President Lula's government approval following the 'Dark Horse' case, with 32% of Brazilians rating the administration as excellent or good, 38% as poor or terrible, and 28% as fair. Despite the uptick, overall evaluation remains negative, highlighting ongoing polarization in public opinion about Lula's performance.

item.title: Governo Lula reduz em 15,5% os gastos com a Marinha
item.description: The Lula government reduced naval spending by 15.5% between 2023 and 2025 compared to the same period under Bolsonaro, based on inflation-adjusted data from March 2026. Despite the budget cut, the Navy received strategic focus with the delivery of Brazil’s first domestically built frigate since 1980 (F200 Tamandaré) and new orders for German-made frigates, driven by the need to secure maritime routes amid the Iran crisis and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
